blocks.h: Where endotoxin gets in, and what we design against
blocks.intro: Endotoxin is heat stable: sanitization kills bacteria but not what they already released. So we design out the places biofilm grows.

items.d: Double tubesheet exchangers, drainable layout, scheduled hot sanitization, a sample point after each cooler.
Loop and pump sized to the batch schedule; return flow alarmed; turbulent flow as EU GMP Annex 1, 6.9 requires.
Every branch to L/D ≤ 2 to ASME BPE; future tie-ins as valved points, not capped stubs.

items.t: Ambient PW ahead of the generator
items.d: Where most biofilm lives. Hot water or ozone sanitization on a stated schedule.
Integrity testing, continuous TOC and conductivity, and the control strategy the EMA expects for non-distillation WFI.

blocks.h: Decisions to settle before the user requirement specification (URS)

items.d: Storage and loop flow sized from how many buffer and media preparations overlap, and how fast they draw.

items.t: Hot loop with cool outlets, or ambient
items.d: Hot WFI suits CIP, but each cool outlet needs a cooler. Ozonated ambient loops need proven ozone removal before use.
Both are pharmacopoeial. Distillation has the longer inspection record; membrane uses no plant steam but needs a stronger control strategy.

items.t: How single-use your process really is
items.d: Single-use cuts CIP and SIP water; media, buffers, autoclaves and stainless vessels still need WFI and pure steam.

items.t: Make media and buffers, or buy them
items.d: Bought liquid concentrates move WFI demand off site; hydrating powder in-house adds it to your peak.
Feed swings from near freezing to over 20 °C; some supplies use chloramine. We size membranes for your coldest month.

blocks.h: Questions biologics process, validation and QA leads ask

items.q: We are a start-up with one clinical product. Is a full WFI system justified?
items.a: Not always. Purchased bulk WFI or a compact membrane WFI skid ([membrane WFI skid lead time, weeks]) can carry a clinical programme, with PW and pure steam on site. What matters is that the tank, loop and space you build now take the commercial train later. We set out both routes with costs and qualification scope.

items.q: Our facility is single-use. Do we still need WFI and pure steam?
items.a: Usually yes. Media and buffers made in-house need WFI, autoclaves need pure steam, and most single-use plants keep some stainless tanks for buffer preparation that need CIP and SIP. Demand is lower and peakier than in a stainless plant, which often favours smaller generation and more storage.

items.q: How do you control endotoxin at cooled points of use?
items.a: With sanitizable double tubesheet coolers, drainable layout, a hot sanitization step on a schedule we justify from qualification data, and a sample point after each cooler. Endotoxin and microbial samples are taken at every outlet during qualification, in the way production draws water.

items.q: Can a cell therapy or university ATMP facility run on PW or DI water?
items.a: For lab support, glassware washers and autoclave feed, often yes. The EMA guideline sets WFI as the minimum for every step of a cell-based ATMP that is not sterilized afterwards, so water that touches those products is WFI, made on site or bought in. We size each grade to what it supplies.

items.q: Will the qualification we do for clinical supply carry into commercial production?
items.a: Most of it, if the design allowed for growth. Added generation and new points of use go through change control, with a risk assessment that sets the scope: usually installation and operational qualification (IQ and OQ) for the new section and a period of increased sampling. We state that scope before work starts.

items.q: Is membrane WFI acceptable for biologics?
items.a: USP allows WFI by distillation or a process shown equivalent or superior to it; Ph. Eur. 0169 has allowed reverse osmosis with other techniques since April 2017. For EU markets, notice goes to the GMP supervisory authority before use, and some corporate standards still require distillation. Confirm product by product with your regulatory team.
